scenes.heading: Terraform State, Modules & Workspaces
scenes.subheading: Scaling Terraform across teams and environments
scenes.narration: As Terraform grows, three concepts become essential: state, modules, and workspaces.

scenes.heading: The three pillars
bullets: State: the source of truth for real resources
Remote backend: shared state with locking
scenes.narration: State is Terraform's source of truth, mapping your code to the resources that actually exist. A remote backend stores that state centrally and locks it so two people cannot corrupt it at once. Modules package infrastructure into reusable, composable units. And workspaces give you isolated state so the same configuration can manage separate environments.

scenes.heading: Remote state and a module
scenes.narration: The backend block moves state into an S3 bucket and uses a DynamoDB table for locking, so a whole team can collaborate without clobbering each other. The module block reuses a warehouse module and passes in variables, including the current workspace name, which lets the same code produce a development or production warehouse depending on which workspace is active.

scenes.heading: Local vs remote state
scenes.narration: Local state lives as a file on a single laptop with no locking, so it is easily lost and dangerous for teams. Remote state moves that file to a shared, durable store that locks during every apply, which is the only safe way to run Terraform collaboratively.

scenes.heading: Promoting through workspaces
scenes.narration: You create a workspace such as staging to hold its own isolated state. You apply your configuration there first and validate that everything behaves. Once satisfied, you switch to the production workspace and apply the very same code, promoting a proven configuration between environments.

scenes.text: Protect state with a locking remote backend, factor infrastructure into modules, and isolate environments with workspaces.
scenes.narration: To scale Terraform safely, protect your state with a locking remote backend, factor repeated infrastructure into modules, and isolate each environment with its own workspace.
